egg_development_days_21_23c.conditions: 21-23 C; ad libitum prey in laboratory culture.

protonymph_development_days_21_23c.notes: Mean protonymph duration for successful prey treatments.

deutonymph_development_days_21_23c.notes: Mean deutonymph duration for successful prey treatments.

adult_female_longevity_days_21_23c.notes: Mean total adult female longevity in the cited prey comparison.

total_eggs_per_female_21_23c.notes: Mean total eggs; diet affected pre-oviposition but not this reported total.

fecundity_25c_nematode_prey.notes: Mean total eggs on Meloidogyne juveniles at 25 ± 1 C, illustrating strong condition/prey dependence.

reproduction.notes: Unfertilized females can produce males, while fertilized females produce both sexes; a single mate_required boolean is therefore only a coarse runtime hint.

body_mass.summary: Species example intentionally avoids inventing a body-mass constant; source a direct adult mass before runtime use.

adult_wet_mass_mg.notes: No direct mass measurement is used in this example.

water_dependence.summary: Soil/humus/litter predator; moist culture conditions are standard, but no generic moisture coefficient is frozen.

thermal_response.summary: Development/reproduction are strongly temperature-dependent; exact response curve belongs in species data if the taxon is ever promoted to runtime.

life_table_temperature_c.notes: Temperature of one detailed life-table experiment; not a universal optimum.

notes: EXAMPLE_ONLY: no runtime calibration values are supplied. This profile exists to prove that the schema supports a five-stage mite lifecycle and mixed sexual/arrhenotokous reproduction without changing simulation algorithms.

adult_female_length_mm.notes: Extension-scale rendering anchor; useful for visualization, not a high-confidence morphometric dataset.

render.coloration: Light to pale brown adults; immature stages paler.
stage_differences: Six-legged larva; eight-legged nymphal and adult stages; female larger than male.
render.locomotion_style: Fast substrate walking and prey-search behavior.
reference_images_asset_notes: Taxonomic caution: commercial material historically labeled 'Hypoaspis miles' can be misidentified. Do not encode Hypoaspis miles as an unquestioned synonym of S. scimitus.

sources.notes: Important warning that S. scimitus and S. miles should not be casually conflated.
